title: In the late 1800s, drainage and a new river channel altered Florida's Ocklawaha Prairie
summary_full: The Ocklawaha Prairie Restoration Area spans 6,301 acres in Florida, focused on revitalizing wetlands and promoting wildlife habitats. Key restoration efforts have led to improved water quality and increased capacity for floodwater storage. Complementing these efforts is a Chornobyl Memorial Forest honoring victims of the 1986 nuclear disaster. Visitors can enjoy hiking, fishing, and primitive camping, while seasonal waterfowl hunting adds to the area's recreational appeal.
